jobs.title: Product Manager, Hardware
jobs.description:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a product leader to drive our hardware product portfolio and ship products people love. You'll own the complete product development cycle from concept to launch and beyond. We’re on a mission to give everyone a personal AI companion, and this is your chance to shape that future.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Build products people love by deeply understanding user needs.

• Drive product management for our hardware products, setting vision, strategy, and roadmap.

• Own end-to-end development from prototyping through post-launch updates in market.

• Make difficult decisions about product trade-offs, balancing user priorities and technical constraints.

• Define and track key product metrics to measure success and inform future decisions.
• Help drive the go-to-market, communications, and community strategy in partnership with marketing.

• Lead a small team of product managers, providing mentorship and strategic direction.

• Understand market trends and dynamics that help ensure we always lead from the front.

• Collaborate with engineering, design, operations, and other cross-functional teams to bring the shared vision to life.




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• 6+ years of product management experience.

• Proven track record of successfully launching consumer hardware products.

• Experience managing complex product development cycles from concept to market.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with ability to make make data-informed decisions.

• Experience building and leading lean product management teams.

• Deep understanding of hardware development processes, including prototyping, manufacturing, and supply chain considerations.

• Outstanding communication skills.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• A passion for AI.

• Technical background with ability to engage deeply with engineers.

• Experience building deeply integrated software and hardware experiences.

• Experience with international manufacturing and global supply chain management.



Sesame is committed to a workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered. We welcome all qualified applicants, embracing diversity in race, gender, identity, orientation, ability, and more. We provide reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. Contact careers@sesame.com for assistance.



Full-time Employee Benefits: 

 - 401 (k) max employer match: 3.5% of compensation

 - 100% employer-paid health, vision, and dental benefits for you and your dependents

 - Unlimited PTO and sick time

 - Flexible spending account with employer matching up to $1,650/year (medical FSA)

 - Guardian Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

 - Opportunity to share in the company's success with competitive stock options

Benefits do not apply to contingent/contract workers.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Electrical
jobs.description:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Sesame is integrating a complex sensing and computing system into a compact, attractive wearable form factor. The Electrical TPM owns the program plan for that system: main logic and sensor boards, flex circuits, power and battery, custom silicon, and the sensing subsystems that let the device understand the wearer and their surroundings. You will carry these subsystems from architecture through EVT, DVT and PVT builds, working alongside our Electrical, Silicon, Firmware and Manufacturing teams and our contract manufacturers and component suppliers.



The ideal candidate has an electrical engineering background, has owned board and flex releases through multiple prototype builds, and is comfortable in the details of bring-up, failure analysis and vendor management. You know what it takes to get a board from schematic release to a working unit on a factory line, and you can tell the difference between a risk that needs escalation and one that needs a day of debug.



We are a small team working on very ambitious projects. In a fast-paced startup, everyone must be comfortable, collaborative, decisive, and able to achieve results with limited supervision.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own the electrical program schedule from architecture through EVT, DVT and PVT, including board and flex design releases, bring-up milestones and validation exit criteria.

 - Drive cross-functional execution across Electrical, Silicon, Firmware, Product Design and Manufacturing. Communicate status, risks and decisions clearly to engineers and executives.

 - Program-manage the sensing subsystems: sensor selection, tuning and calibration plans, firmware integration, and factory test, including their interaction with enclosure materials and industrial design.

 - Track DOEs from concept through POR selection

 - Manage board, flex and component suppliers: quotes, POs, demand quantities, delivery schedules, customs and consigned material.

 - Plan electrical materials and build matrices for prototype builds; coordinate SMT and system builds across multiple vendors and factory sites.

 - Run failure analysis triage for electrical issues: every issue has an owner, a due date and a path to closure; the burndown is reviewed regularly.

 - Maintain the electrical section of the program's master issues list and weekly status, aligned with area leads.

 - Track long-lead and end-of-life component risk, and drive mitigation before it affects a build.

 - Travel to contract manufacturer and supplier sites for builds and bring-up as needed.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

 - BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or equivalent practical experience.

 - 5+ years of experience in hardware program management or electrical design of consumer electronics, with at least 2 years managing programs.

 - Hands-on experience releasing PCBs and flex circuits and taking them through prototype builds (EVT/DVT/PVT or equivalent).

 - Working knowledge of sensor integration, power and battery systems, and board-level bring-up and debug.

 - Direct experience managing PCB, SMT and component suppliers, including quotes, POs and delivery schedules.

 - Experience running failure analysis and issue tracking across engineering teams.

 - Strong written communication; able to run a program with clear plans, decision logs and status updates.

 - Ability to travel internationally, up to 25%.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience with wearables or other very small, battery-powered devices.

 - Experience with custom silicon or ASIC programs and their firmware integration.

 - Experience integrating sensors into small, body-worn devices, and the tuning and factory-test challenges that come with it.

 - Experience working with contract manufacturers.

 - Experience with Linear, Arena or similar issue and PLM tools.

 - Startup experience, or ownership of new product programs at a large company.



Sesame is committed to a workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered. We welcome all qualified applicants, embracing diversity in race, gender, identity, orientation, ability, and more. We provide reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. Contact careers@sesame.com for assistance.



Full-time Employee Benefits: 

 - 401 (k) max employer match: 3.5% of compensation

 - 100% employer-paid health, vision, and dental benefits for you and your dependents

 - Unlimited PTO and sick time

 - Flexible spending account with employer matching up to $1,650/year (medical FSA)

 - Guardian Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

 - Opportunity to share in the company's success with competitive stock options

Benefits do not apply to contingent/contract workers.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Product Design
jobs.description:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Sesame is integrating a complex sensing and computing system into a compact wearable that has to be light, comfortable and attractive, and available in many styles and colors. The Product Design TPM owns the program plan for the mechanical side of that product: enclosures and cosmetic parts, materials and finishes, mechanisms, packaging and accessories. You will carry hundreds of mechanical parts through design release, tooling, validation and factory builds, working with our Product Design, Industrial Design, Manufacturing and Operations teams and with our contract manufacturers and tooling and materials suppliers.



The ideal candidate has a mechanical or product design engineering background, has run part release and tooling for a consumer product through EVT, DVT and PVT, and knows how to keep design change under control when the schedule is tight and the design is still moving. You are comfortable telling a designer or an executive what a change will cost in weeks and dollars, and then building the plan that makes it happen.



We are a small team working on very ambitious projects. In a fast-paced startup, everyone must be comfortable, collaborative, decisive, and able to achieve results with limited supervision.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own the Product Design program schedule from concept through EVT, DVT and PVT, including part release, tooling kickoff, first-shots, validation and phase exit criteria.

 - Run the PD release and change-control process: every part has a release date, an owner and a status in our PLM tool.

 - Program-manage styles, colors and materials: cosmetic material qualification, color development, SKU rollout planning.

 - Coordinate design validation and reliability testing for mechanical parts, and own closure of design-review action items.

 - Manage tooling, materials, cosmetic-part and packaging suppliers: quotes, POs, sample requests, tooling timelines and delivery schedules.

 - Plan mechanical materials and build matrices for prototype builds, and lead mechanical build readiness across factory sites.

 - Run failure analysis triage for mechanical and cosmetic issues: every issue has an owner, a due date and a path to closure.

 - Maintain the Product Design section of the program's master issues list and weekly status, aligned with area leads.

 - Travel to contract manufacturer and supplier sites for builds, tooling reviews and validation as needed.
   
   


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

 - BS in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent practical experience.

 - 5+ years of experience in hardware program management or mechanical/product design engineering of consumer electronics, with at least 2 years managing programs.

 - Hands-on experience releasing mechanical parts and taking them through tooling and prototype builds (EVT/DVT/PVT or equivalent).

 - Working knowledge of high-volume manufacturing processes (injection molding, machining, stamping, cosmetic finishing) and tolerance, DFM and validation practices.

 - Direct experience managing tooling, materials or fabrication suppliers, including quotes, POs, samples and schedules.

 - Experience running change control and part release in a PLM tool.

 - Strong written communication; able to run a program with clear plans, decision logs and status updates.

 - Ability to travel internationally, up to 25%.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience with wearables or other products with heavy industrial design and cosmetic constraints.

 - Experience with premium cosmetic materials and finishes and their supply chains.

 - Experience managing many SKUs, colors or configurations through a single program.

 - Experience with packaging or accessories programs.

 - Experience working with contract manufacturers.

 - Experience with Linear, Arena or similar issue and PLM tools.

 - Startup experience, or ownership of new product programs at a large company.
